newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-MCNULTY MASTERS STRONG WINDS TO TAKE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY MASTERS STRONG WINDS TO TAKE LEAD.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty mastered howling winds to open up a four-shot lead in the third round of the Wild Coast Challenge on Saturday.
The 43-year-old world number 18, two shots behind overnight leader Desvonde Botes of South Africa, collected four birdies and four bogeys for a level-par 70 and a three-round total of 204.
With the north-easterly blowing at around 30 knots, McNulty moved to six-under for the tournament as he closed in on his third successive win of the South African tour.
"It was really tough out there today and the winds were about as strong as they can get here," McNulty said. "Our round took over six hours and it was a lot of hard work.

"The course was set up fairly tough as well and it was often a lottery as far as club selection was concerned. But I played very well today -- missing a few birdie opportunities and enjoying one or two lucky breaks."
Botes slipped back into second place on 208 after a 76 while fellow South African James Kingston moved up to third place on 209 after a steady round of 70.

Only two players broke par in the challenging conditions. American-based South African Ronnie McCann carded a two-under-par 68 early in the day to have a share of 11th place on 214 and Irishman John McHenry returned a 69 to share fourth place on 211.
